newsitem.title: PERU: Two bus crashes kill 17, injure 33 in Peru.
newsitem.headline: Two bus crashes kill 17, injure 33 in Peru.

text.p: Two bus accidents killed 17 people and left another 33 injured along Peru's southern coast and in the central Andes, authorities said on Monday.

A bus slammed into a minivan late on Sunday killing 13 people, including five children, and seriously injuring three more near the Andean town of Huancayo, 195 miles (310 km) east of Lima, as the two vehicles snaked along a mountain road in the dark.
A local fireman said all the victims were travelling aboard the smaller vehicle, which was was carrying 16 passengers.

There were no reports of injuries among the 50 passengers aboard the larger bus, which was travelling from the highland town of Hunacavelica to the capital. Police said they suspect the accident was caused by drunkenness of the van's driver.
Earlier on Sunday, four passengers died when a bus swerved to avoid colliding with another vehicle, skidded off a highway and flipped, a bus company employee said.
Another 31 were injured in the crash on the Panamerican Highway near the city of Moquegua, 700 miles (1,117 kms) south of Lima, a bus company employee said.
The frequency of road crashes in Peru has brought calls for tighter transport regulations.
